answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by charging a real cost at every inlet where new identities enter: each agent must stake funds or burn compute before it can earn, so a flood of fake agents faces a gale of expenses that grows with every sockpuppet. Meanwhile reputation accrues slowly — trust is earned through verified work, not bought — so attackers cannot simply wander in, claim rewards, and vanish. The math turns against them: each fake identity costs more to create and maintain than it can ever extract.
